title: Constructible internal Hom over a regular base of dimension at most one
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian regular scheme of Krull dimension at most one [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $S$. Let $X\to S$ be separated of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $A=\mathbf F_\ell$ and use ordinary small-etale derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For every $M,N\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], the derived internal sheaf Hom satisfies
$$R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$$
[def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. No dualizing object, biduality, potential pinning, or purity hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 3.15, regular-base alternative (a), for constructibility; Proposition 3.14 with Proposition 2.29(1) for bounded Tor amplitude, specialized to the field A=F_ell. Independent low-dimensional finiteness input also stated in ILO Expose XIII Theorem 2.3.1(i); finite-dimensional cohomological bound in Expose XVIII-A Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.4. The regular-base case uses classical dimension-at-most-one finiteness, not the quasi-excellent/Gabber alternative or the dualizing results in section 3.

proof.text: First record closure under finite derived constructions. By [thm-constructible-serre], constructible $A$-module sheaves are closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions. Applying [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory] to this subcategory shows that $D^b_c$ is triangulated. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X$ is Noetherian. We prove the assertion simultaneously for all closed subschemes $T\hookrightarrow X$, by induction on their underlying closed subsets: the induction claim at a closed subset quantifies over all closed subschemes with that support, including thickenings. The empty case is zero. Quotients of Noetherian rings are Noetherian, and generators for a finite-type algebra still generate its quotients; hence these closed subschemes are again Noetherian and of finite type over the same $S$. Their diagonals are restrictions of the closed diagonal of $X/S$, so they remain separated. Fix such a nonempty $T$, assume the assertion for every proper closed support, and fix $M,N\in D^b_c(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$.

source.place: Propositions 3.9 and 3.15; Noetherian devissage expanded without a dualizing object.

proof.text: For any open immersion $v:W\hookrightarrow T$, the input [lem-per-low-base-open-sheaf-finiteness] gives $Rv_*F\in D^b_c(T,A)$ for every constructible sheaf $F$ in degree zero. This extends to every $L\in D^b_c(W,A)$: its finitely many truncation triangles [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] express it as successive extensions of $H^q(L)[-q]$. Module-sheaf categories have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], so [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] applies to their additive left exact direct image. Apply $Rv_*$ to those finitely many triangles and use Step 1. Only finitely many sheaf-dependent bounds occur, so taking their maximum after shifts gives a finite bound. This step does not require a uniform cohomological-dimension estimate for all sheaves.

source.place: Propositions 3.15 and 3.16(1); ILO XIII Theorem 2.3.1(i), p.197; finite Postnikov devissage.

proof.text: There are finitely many nonzero $H^q(M)$. Apply [prop-constructible-generic-constancy] to each and intersect the finitely many dense opens, obtaining a dense open $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ on which every $H^q(M)$ is finite locally constant. The intersection is dense since $T$ is Noetherian and each open contains every generic point of its finitely many irreducible components. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be the reduced closed complement; its support is proper. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], restriction commutes with cohomology, and [prop-constructible-pullback] preserves constructibility. Thus $j^*M,j^*N,i^*M$ are bounded constructible, with the stated locally constant cohomology for $j^*M$.

source.place: Proposition 3.15, open/closed devissage underlying the regular-base case.

proof.text: Here is the local calculation on $U$. If $F$ is a finite locally constant $A$-module sheaf and $G$ a constructible one, then on an etale cover trivializing $F$ it is $A^{\oplus r}$, since $A$ is a field. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] the Hom complex from $A^{\oplus r}[0]$ into a K-injective representative of $G[0]$ is that representative to the finite power $r$; its only cohomology is $G^{\oplus r}$ in degree zero. Restriction of derived Hom to these slice sites agrees with derived Hom there by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Thus all higher internal Ext vanish, and the degree-zero Hom is constructible: on a common stratification trivializing $G$, further etale covers trivialize both sheaves and their Hom is a finite-dimensional constant vector space. Descending these local identifications is exactly finite local constancy on each stratum.

source.place: Proposition 3.15; elementary finite-free internal-Hom calculation on etale slices.

proof.text: Apply the finite truncation triangles [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] first to $j^*N$ and then to $j^*M$. The distinguished-triangle assertions of [lem-sf-hom-triangulated] and Step 4 express $B=R\mathcal Hom_A(j^*M,j^*N)$ as finitely many extensions of bounded constructible objects. Explicitly, if $M$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$ and $N$ in $[c,d]$, the building block $R\mathcal Hom_A(H^q(j^*M)[-q],H^r(j^*N)[-r])$ has its only cohomology in degree $r-q$; hence all blocks lie in $[c-b,d-a]$. The long exact cohomology sequence and the Serre property from Step 1 give constructibility and the same finite bound for $B$. Step 2 then gives $Rj_*B\in D^b_c(T,A)$.

source.place: Proposition 3.15; finite truncation devissage, and Proposition 3.16(1) for the open term.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-per-etale-internal-hom-localization] with first argument $A_T[0]$ and second argument $N$. The identity $R\mathcal Hom_A(A_W,L)=L$, computed directly from [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], for $W=T,U,Z$, identifies its triangle with
$$i_*Ri^!N\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*N\longrightarrow(i_*Ri^!N)[1].$$
Both middle and right terms are bounded constructible by Step 2, so Step 1 gives $i_*Ri^!N\in D^b_c(T,A)$. The counit $i^*i_*\cong1$ of [prop-openclosed-lowerstar-fully-faithful] is module-linear by naturality with respect to the $A$-actions, and applies termwise. Exactness of $i^*$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and constructible pullback [prop-constructible-pullback] therefore imply $Ri^!N\cong i^*i_*Ri^!N\in D^b_c(Z,A)$. This proves the needed exceptional-restriction finiteness from open direct-image finiteness; no purity theorem is invoked.

source.place: ILO XVII proof of Lemma 7.6.10, displayed triangle p.313, applied to the constant first argument; Zheng Proposition 3.16(2), closed case.

proof.text:
Since $Z$ has proper closed support, the simultaneous induction hypothesis applies to $i^*M$ and $Ri^!N$ on $Z$, giving $C=R\mathcal Hom_A(i^*M,Ri^!N)\in D^b_c(Z,A)$. The exactness of closed direct image is part of [lem-per-etale-internal-hom-localization]. Its preservation of constructible cohomology follows from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-constructible-noetherian], applied to the finite closed immersion; the underlying finite sheaves and their $A$-actions give precisely the constant-$A$ constructibility condition. Thus $i_*C$ is bounded constructible. Apply [lem-per-etale-internal-hom-localization] now with first argument $M$ and second argument $N$:
$$i_*C\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)\longrightarrow Rj_*B\longrightarrow(i_*C)[1].$$
Step 5 gives the right term, and Step 1 gives bounded constructibility of the middle term. This completes the Noetherian induction, including $T=X$, and proves the exact item statement.

source.place: Proposition 3.15; ILO XVII proof of Lemma 7.6.10, p.313, open/closed internal-Hom triangle.

proof_origin.place: Propositions 3.14–3.16, pp.18–19; explicit finite-field Noetherian devissage using ILO XIII 2.3.1(i) and the purely formal triangle in ILO XVII 7.6.10. No dualizing argument.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q39-3635ae085 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read both files in full, every cited statement, ILO XIII 2.3.1 (printed p.197) and Zheng 3.14–3.16 (pp.18–19). The item statement and stmt_deps are identical to the live node, which is still unsplit. New node lem-per-low-base-open-sheaf-finiteness: R^q j_* of a constructible F_ell-module sheaf is constructible and bounded per sheaf, over a regular Noetherian base of dimension <=1. It is a special case of ILO XIII 2.3.1(i), which needs only S Noetherian of dimension 1. The dimension-0 case via S ⊔ Spec Q[t] is valid, and Zheng 3.16(1) states the same. B1–B9 hold: statement only, objects introduced, defs correct, six searches recorded. It is not a duplicate of lem-per-gabber-open-immersion-sheaf-finiteness, which needs quasi-excellence that fails for a non-excellent DVR. Proof steps: Step 1 sets up a valid Noetherian induction over closed subsets, with D^b_c triangulated via thm-constructible-serre and the weak-Serre lemma. Step 2 gives finitely many per-sheaf bounds through truncation triangles and Rv_* triangulated. Step 3 uses generic constancy; for F_ell, abelian and module local constancy coincide. Step 4 is a genuinely elementary finite-free RHom calculation on slices. Step 5's degree bound [c-b, d-a] checks out. Step 6 applies the localization triangle with K=A_T to give i_*Ri^!N, then uses i^*i_*≅1 and exact i^* to show Ri^!N ∈ D^b_c(Z). Step 7 applies the induction on Z, finite pushforward and the localization triangle, which closes the induction. No SGA citation and no purity or dualizing input. The tool_uses are all generic and accepted. The parent's use on (P^1)^n over a field or an excellent DVR is covered. Edge cases checked: empty X, Z empty, field base, non-excellent DVR, nonreduced X. No fixes.
